3. The case of the plainitiffs, in short, is that lands of CS Khatian No. 82 corresponding to SA Khatian No.116 originally belonged to Aviram Sarder and Rupchan Sarder and others and predecessors of the plaintiffs were bargaders under the said owners and their names were recorded as such bargaders in the CS Khatian. Their further case is that Aviram died leaving son Guru Charan Ram Kanta and Rup Chand died leaving sons Ram Krishna and Ram Charan and they settled the suit land on 17-5-1939 with Arjun, Fakir, Sanatan Jageswar and Chandra Kanta by accepting a Kabuliyat and since then the said tenants possessed the suit land and thereafter they died leaving the "plaintiffs as their heirs. Plaintiffs" further case is that on 1-11-86 defendants threatened the plaintiffs with dispossession from the suit land and hence they field Title Suit No. 78 of 1986 and defendants filed a written statement on 27-6-87 and disclosed that the suit lands were auction purchased by their predecessors on 16-9-1941. Therefore, they filed the present suit challenging the aforesaid auction sale and all other related proceedings upon which the defendants based their claim in the suit land. 

 8. In this case there is no dispute that Arun and others predecessors of the plaintiffs took settlement of the suit land from Ram Charan and others by Kabuliyat dated 17-5-39 Ext.2. Plaintiffs claimed the suit land on the basis of the said settlement. On the other hand, defendants claimed that the suit land was auction sold on 16-9-1941 in Rent Execution case No.827 of 1941 and auction purchased by Ram Charan and others, the predecessors of some of the defendants. Ext Ka is the certified copy of the decree passed on 11-6-1941 in Rent Suit No.676 of 1941 filed by Ram Charan Sardar and others against Arjun Mondal and others. Ext. Kha is the certified copy of the sale certificate dated 26-11-1941 by which the said Ram Charan Sardar and others purchased the suit land. Ext. Kha (1) is the writ of delivery of possession by which possession was delivered to the said auction purchasers on 14-12-1941. Ext. Ga is the certified copy of case register of Mise-judicial case register which shows that Jageswar Mondal one of the tenants filed Miscellaneous Case No.178 on 28-5-42 under section 174(3) of the Bengal Tenancy Act for setting aside the sale held on 16-9-1941 in Rent Execution case No.827 of 1941 against Ram Charan Sarder and others and the said case was dismissed on contest on 15-2-43. Ext. Cha is the certified copy of the order in Misc. Case No.275 of 1941 filed by Chandra Mondal against Ram Charan Sarder and the said order shows that the Misc. Case was dismissed on contest with cost. Ext. Gha (1) is the certified copy of order passed in Misc. Appeal No.69 of 1942 filed by Chandra MondaI against Ram Charan Sarder which shows that the said Misc. Appeal was also dismissed on contest. Besides the aforesaid documents defendants also produced and proved certain other documents such as rent receipts, Ext Cha series and information slip, Ext Chha, Kabala Ext. Ka (1), certified copy of mutation khatian Ext. Kha (1) and Kha 1(1), rent receipts Ext Ga(1) series, certified copy of certain orders in Title Suit No. 78 of 1976, and vested property rent receipts. Court of appeal below did not at all consider the aforesaid documents along with oral evidence on record to decide whether plaintiffs' raiyati interest in the suit land still subsist or not. None of the courts below also considered the absence of payment of rent by the plaintiffs from the date of alleged auction upto the date of filing the suit and effect of the writ of delivery of possession Ext. Kha(1). The record of the vested property case could be marked Ext. by the appellate Court if any of the parties filed an application for accepting the same as additional evidence. Court of appeal below merely shirked its responsibility in deciding the appeal without at all looking into oral or documentary evidence on record. This kind of shirking responsibility is highly deprecable. Court of appeal below being the last court of fact should consider all materials on record and is at liberty either to affirm or set aside the judgment and decree of the trial Court after assigning reasons therefor. Court of appeal below in this case having not done so, I find merit on the submission of the learned Advocate for the petitioner.
